question: Recent reports indicate a substantial increase in illegal arrivals on the Balearic Islands from Algeria. While these arrivals take place on Spanish territory, questions arise on the subsequent distribution of these migrants within the European Union, and on whether this occurs through official mechanisms or through onward movements. 1.

Have migrants who initially entered the European Union via the Algeria–Balearic Islands route been relocated or transferred to other Member States under EU solidarity mechanisms, voluntary relocation schemes or comparable arrangements, and if so, in what numbers and to which Member States?

Does the Commission possess data, estimates or assessments concerning subsequent secondary movements of migrants arriving via this route to other Member States, and if so, which Member States are identified as the principal destinations?

Taking into account both relocations and secondary movements, how does the Commission assess the overall impact of the Algeria–Balearic Islands route on migration pressures in Member States other than Spain, and what effect does it expect the Migration and Asylum Pact to have on these movements?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2026) With the Asylum and Migration Management Regulation (AMMR)1, which entered into application on 12 June 2026, a permanent and flexible solidarity mechanism is in place.

Following the Commission's assessment covering the period July 2024 – June 20252, Spain was identified as a Member State under migratory pressure and is eligible to benefit from the Solidarity Pool agreed by the Council in December 20253. The solidarity mechanism does not operate on the basis of specific migratory routes.

Information on the implementation of solidarity measures will be reported by Member States to the EU Solidarity Coordinator in accordance with Article 60(6) of the AMMR. The second Annual Report that the Commission will adopt in October 2026 will present the state of implementation of the Pact on Migration and Asylum, including the solidarity mechanism4.

The Commission regularly monitors secondary movements and, when assessing whether a Member State is under migratory pressure, at risk thereof or facing a significant migratory situation, takes into account a range of indicators, including asylum applications, outgoing take back requests as well as outgoing take charge requests based on illegal entry and stay5.
The Commission has no specific information on secondary movements from the Balearic Islands to other Member States.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 on asylum and

migration management, amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1147 and (EU) 2021/1060 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 604/2013. 2 Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2323 of 11 November 2025 pursuant to Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of the European Parliament and of the Council. 3 Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2642 of 22 December 2025 on the establishment of the Annual Solidarity Pool for 2026.

4 https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/policies/migration-and-asylum/pact-migration-and-asylum/implementingpact-migration-and-asylum_en. 5 Commission Staff Working Document, SWD(2025) 792 final, Methodology for the purposes of Commission implementing decision pursuant to Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of the European Parliament and of the Council; https://home-affairs.ec.europa.
